web.files.column.name.note: Files: column heading in the folder's list and in the search results.

web.files.column.size.note: Files: column heading in the folder's list and in the search results.

web.files.gallery.download_all.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): button that downloads every photo and video of the gallery.

web.files.gallery.download_count.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): button that downloads the selected photos and videos. {count} is how many are selected.

web.files.gallery.meta.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): under the title. {count} is how many photos and videos, {size} their size with its unit (4.6 GB).

web.files.gallery.meta_until.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): under the title. {count} is how many photos and videos, {size} their size with its unit (4.6 GB); {date} is when the link stops working, already formatted (7 October 2026).

web.files.gallery.next.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): accessibility name of the viewer's button that shows the next photo or video.

web.files.gallery.not_found.text: This link doesn't exist or has expired.

web.files.gallery.open_failed.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): error when the gallery couldn't be opened.

web.files.gallery.opening.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): while the gallery opens.

web.files.gallery.position.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): the viewer's title. {name} is the file's name, {index} its position and {total} how many there are.

web.files.gallery.previous.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): accessibility name of the viewer's button that shows the previous photo or video.

web.files.gallery.select_all.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): button while selecting photos to download.

web.files.gallery.stopped.text: The device stopped sending the file.
web.files.gallery.stopped.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): error when a download stopped half way.

web.files.gallery.title.note: A shared gallery's page, seen by anyone with its link (visitors with no account; in their browser's language): the page's title and heading when the gallery has no description.

web.files.keep_out.banner.note: Files: banner over a folder kept out of Images. A folder kept out of Images: its photos and videos aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images; Files still shows them. Use the same name for Images as web.shell.menu.images.

web.files.keep_out.banner_parent.text: Inside {folder}, which is kept out of Images - photos and videos here aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images.

Keep “{name}” out of Images?

Its photos and videos won't be tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images, and the tags and faces already found in them are deleted. Files still shows them.
web.files.keep_out.confirm_keep.note: Files: confirmation (title, blank line, message) before keeping a folder out of Images. {name} is the folder's name. The tags and faces found in its photos are deleted. Write the quotes in your language's style. A folder kept out of Images: its photos and videos aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images; Files still shows them. Use the same name for Images as web.shell.menu.images.

web.files.keep_out.confirm_show.text:
Show “{name}” in Images?

Its photos and videos go back to Images, and are tagged - and searched for faces, if face recognition is on - in the background.
web.files.keep_out.confirm_show.note: Files: confirmation (title, blank line, message) before showing a folder kept out of Images in Images again; its photos are then searched for faces when face recognition is on. {name} is the folder's name. Write the quotes in your language's style. A folder kept out of Images: its photos and videos aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images; Files still shows them. Use the same name for Images as web.shell.menu.images.

web.files.keep_out.kept.note: Files: read out by screen readers once a folder is kept out of Images. {name} is the folder's name.

web.files.keep_out.parent_tip.text: Inside {folder}, which is kept out of Images
web.files.keep_out.parent_tip.note: Files: tooltip and accessibility name of the crossed-out picture beside a folder that is kept out because a folder above it is. {folder} is that folder's path. web.files.keep_out.show.note: Files: button on the banner of a folder kept out of Images that shows its photos in Images again. A folder kept out of Images: its photos and videos aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images; Files still shows them. Use the same name for Images as web.shell.menu.images.

web.files.keep_out.show_named.note: Files: button on the banner of a folder inside one kept out of Images; it shows that outer folder ({name}) in Images again. Use the same name for Images as web.shell.menu.images.

web.files.keep_out.shown.note: Files: read out by screen readers once a folder kept out of Images is shown in Images again. {name} is the folder's name.

web.files.keep_out.state.note: Files: tooltip of the crossed-out picture beside a search result kept out of Images. web.files.keep_out.switch.note: Files: accessibility name of the crossed-out picture button beside a folder; screen readers add whether it is pressed (kept out). {name} is the folder's name. web.files.keep_out.tip_off.text: Keep out of Images: photos and videos here won't be tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images
web.files.keep_out.tip_off.note: Files: tooltip of the switch beside a folder shown in Images. A folder kept out of Images: its photos and videos aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images; Files still shows them. Use the same name for Images as web.shell.menu.images.

web.files.keep_out.tip_on.text: Kept out of Images: photos and videos here aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images. Click to show them in Images.
web.files.keep_out.tip_on.note: Files: tooltip of the switch beside a folder kept out of Images. A folder kept out of Images: its photos and videos aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images; Files still shows them. Use the same name for Images as web.shell.menu.images.

web.files.links.confirm_delete.text: Delete this link? The shared copies are deleted and the link stops working.

web.files.links.delete_failed.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: error when the device couldn't delete a link and gave no reason of its own.

web.files.links.details.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: details of a link. {size} is the space its copy takes (4.6 GB), {made} when it was made and {until} when it stops working, already formatted (7 Oct 2026, 14:05).

web.files.links.details_files.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: details of a link. {size} is the space its copy takes (4.6 GB), {made} when it was made and {until} when it stops working, already formatted (7 Oct 2026, 14:05); {count} is how many files it shares.

web.files.links.gallery.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: the name of a gallery link that has no description.

web.files.links.hint.text: Galleries and downloads you shared. The links themselves aren't kept on the device, so they can't be shown again - only removed.
web.files.links.hint.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: explanation under the title.

web.files.links.load_failed.text: Could not load the shared links.
web.files.links.load_failed.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: error when the device couldn't list them and gave no reason of its own.

web.files.links.never_opened.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: a link nobody has opened yet.

web.files.links.none.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: when nothing is shared.

web.files.links.opened.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: how often a link was opened, and when last ({date}, already formatted: 7 Oct 2026, 14:05).

web.files.links.title.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: the section's title.

web.files.links.total.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: after the explanation, the space all the shared copies take. {size} has its unit (4.6 GB).

web.files.links.zip.note: Settings > Shared Links: every gallery and download link shared: the name of a link to a ZIP of files that has no description.

web.files.list.contents.note: Files: accessibility name of the region that lists the folder's contents. {folder} is the folder's path (/Photos/2024/).

web.files.list.empty.note: Files: in the grid when the folder has nothing in it.

web.files.list.list_failed.note: Files: error when the device couldn't list the folder and gave no reason of its own.

web.files.list.opening.note: Files: in place of a file's name, or over its thumbnail, while the file is fetched from the device to open it.

web.files.list.select_item.note: Files: accessibility name of the tick box on a file or folder, in the list and in the grid. {name} is its name.

web.files.list.tip.text: Tip: Drag files here to upload to {folder}.
web.files.list.tip.note: Files: hint under the folder's contents. {folder} is the folder's path (/Photos/), shown in a code font (<code>).

web.files.list.total.note: Files: under the toolbar, how many entries the folder shows ({count}, in bold <b>).

web.files.list.unexpected.note: Files: error when the device answered the folder listing with something else than a list.

web.files.list.update_failed.note: Files: message when the device refused or didn't answer a change to a folder (upload only, or kept out of Images) and gave no reason of its own.

web.files.list.upload_only_refused.text: {name} is in an upload-only folder and cannot be deleted.
web.files.list.upload_only_refused.note: Files: message when the device refused to delete a file or folder because it is inside an upload-only folder. {name} is its name.

web.files.list.video.note: Files: accessibility name of the play badge on a video's thumbnail in the grid.

web.files.lock.clear.note: Files: accessibility name of the closed lock on an upload-only folder; clicking it makes the folder normal again. An upload-only folder keeps every file: nothing in it can be deleted, and uploading a file again keeps the old version.

web.files.lock.file.text: In an upload-only folder: cannot be deleted
web.files.lock.file.note: Files list: tooltip and accessibility name of the lock beside a file inside an upload-only folder.

web.files.lock.make.note: Files: tooltip and accessibility name of the open lock on a folder that isn't upload only; clicking it makes it so. An upload-only folder keeps every file: nothing in it can be deleted, and uploading a file again keeps the old version.

web.files.lock.off_tip.text: Make upload only: nothing in this folder can be deleted, and re-uploads keep the old version
web.files.lock.off_tip.note: Files list: tooltip of the open lock on a folder that isn't upload only.

web.files.lock.on_tip.text: Upload only: nothing in this folder can be deleted, and re-uploads keep the old version. Click to clear.
web.files.lock.on_tip.note: Files list: tooltip of the closed lock on an upload-only folder.

web.files.lock.on_tip_short.note: Files grid: tooltip of the lock on a folder that is upload only. An upload-only folder keeps every file: nothing in it can be deleted, and uploading a file again keeps the old version.

web.files.results.back.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): button that leaves the results and goes back to the folder shown before. {folder} is that folder's name.

web.files.results.back_files.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): button that leaves the results and goes back to the top folder of Files.

web.files.results.cant_search.text: This device can't search its files yet. Update it in Settings.
web.files.results.cant_search.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): the device's software is too old to search files.

web.files.results.count.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): how many were found, above the list.

web.files.results.file_kept_out.text: {name}, file in {folder}, kept out of Images
web.files.results.file_kept_out.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): what a screen reader says for a result. {name} is its name, {folder} the folder it is in (/Photos/2024); the file is in a folder kept out of Images.

web.files.results.first.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): above the list when it holds the most the device answers ({limit}: 50).

web.files.results.folder_kept_out.text: {name}, folder in {folder}, kept out of Images
web.files.results.folder_kept_out.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): what a screen reader says for a result. {name} is its name, {folder} the folder it is in (/Photos/2024); the folder is kept out of Images (its photos aren't tagged, searched for faces or shown in Images).

web.files.results.list.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): accessibility name of the list of results. {text} is what was searched for.

web.files.results.no_answer.text: The device didn't answer the search.
web.files.results.no_answer.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): error when the device answered without results or a reason of its own.

web.files.results.none_for.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): read out by screen readers when nothing was found. {text} is what was searched for.

web.files.results.nothing.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): when nothing was found. {text} is what was searched for. Write the quotes in your language's style.

web.files.results.photo_kept_out.text: {name}, photo in {folder}, kept out of Images
web.files.results.photo_kept_out.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): what a screen reader says for a result. {name} is its name, {folder} the folder it is in (/Photos/2024); the photo is in a folder kept out of Images.

web.files.results.searching.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): while the search runs.

web.files.results.searching_for.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): read out by screen readers while the search runs. {text} is what was searched for.

web.files.results.title.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): title. {text} is what was searched for. Write the quotes in your language's style.

web.files.results.unreachable.text: The search didn't reach the device. Check the connection and try again.
web.files.results.unreachable.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): error when the search couldn't be sent.

web.files.results.video_kept_out.text: {name}, video in {folder}, kept out of Images
web.files.results.video_kept_out.note: Files, the results of a search of every file and folder name (from the top bar's Search documents): what a screen reader says for a result. {name} is its name, {folder} the folder it is in (/Photos/2024); the video is in a folder kept out of Images.

web.files.selection.clear.note: Screen-reader name and tooltip of the × at the start of the selection bar in Files: it unselects everything and closes the selection.

text.one: Delete {count} item? This cannot be undone.
text.other: Delete {count} items? This cannot be undone.

web.files.selection.upload_only.text: The selection includes an upload-only folder's contents, which cannot be deleted
web.files.selection.upload_only.note: Files: tooltip of the greyed-out Delete button when something ticked is inside an upload-only folder (a folder whose files can't be deleted).

web.files.share.copy.note: Share as a gallery dialog (from Files or Images): the device copies the photos and videos, re-encrypted with a key only the link carries, and shows the link once: button that copies the link.

web.files.share.days.note: Share as a gallery dialog (from Files or Images): the device copies the photos and videos, re-encrypted with a key only the link carries, and shows the link once: a choice of how long the link works (1, 7 or 30 days).

web.files.share.description.note: Share as a gallery dialog (from Files or Images): the device copies the photos and videos, re-encrypted with a key only the link carries, and shows the link once: label of the gallery's description field.

web.files.share.link.note: Share as a gallery dialog (from Files or Images): the device copies the photos and videos, re-encrypted with a key only the link carries, and shows the link once: accessibility name of the field holding the gallery's link.

web.files.share.preview_failed.text: Could not look at what to share.

web.files.share.title.note: Share as a gallery dialog (from Files or Images): the device copies the photos and videos, re-encrypted with a key only the link carries, and shows the link once: the dialog's title and accessibility name.

web.files.size.gb.note: A size in gigabytes, in Files' lists, the share dialog, Settings > Shared Links and a shared gallery's page. Write your language's symbol (French: Go). {size} is the number, already formatted with its decimals (512, 4.6).

web.files.size.kb.note: A size in kilobytes (1024 bytes), in Files' lists, the share dialog, Settings > Shared Links and a shared gallery's page. Write your language's symbol (French: Ko). {size} is the number, already formatted with its decimals (512, 4.6).

web.files.size.mb.note: A size in megabytes, in Files' lists, the share dialog, Settings > Shared Links and a shared gallery's page. Write your language's symbol (French: Mo). {size} is the number, already formatted with its decimals (512, 4.6).

web.files.sort.created_asc.note: Files: an order in the Sort by list beside the List/Grid switch, and the tooltip of the column heading while the list is in that order. By when the file was created, the oldest first. Name, Size, Created and Modified are the list's column headings (web.files.column.*), written the same way here. Folders always stay above the files, whatever the order.

web.files.sort.created_desc.note: Files: an order in the Sort by list beside the List/Grid switch, and the tooltip of the column heading while the list is in that order. By when the file was created, the newest first. Name, Size, Created and Modified are the list's column headings (web.files.column.*), written the same way here. Folders always stay above the files, whatever the order.

web.files.sort.label.note: Files: label of the drop-down list beside the List/Grid switch (over a folder and over a search's results) that picks the order of the files and folders; also its accessibility name. The orders it lists are web.files.sort.name_asc and the others.

web.files.sort.modified_asc.note: Files: an order in the Sort by list beside the List/Grid switch, and the tooltip of the column heading while the list is in that order. By when the file last changed, the least recent first. Name, Size, Created and Modified are the list's column headings (web.files.column.*), written the same way here. Folders always stay above the files, whatever the order.

web.files.sort.modified_desc.note: Files: an order in the Sort by list beside the List/Grid switch, and the tooltip of the column heading while the list is in that order. By when the file last changed, the most recent first. Name, Size, Created and Modified are the list's column headings (web.files.column.*), written the same way here. Folders always stay above the files, whatever the order.

web.files.sort.name_asc.note: Files: an order in the Sort by list beside the List/Grid switch, and the tooltip of the column heading while the list is in that order. By name, from A to Z (numbers in names in counting order: file2 before file10). Name, Size, Created and Modified are the list's column headings (web.files.column.*), written the same way here. Folders always stay above the files, whatever the order.

web.files.sort.name_desc.note: Files: an order in the Sort by list beside the List/Grid switch, and the tooltip of the column heading while the list is in that order. By name, from Z to A. Name, Size, Created and Modified are the list's column headings (web.files.column.*), written the same way here. Folders always stay above the files, whatever the order.

web.files.sort.size_asc.note: Files: an order in the Sort by list beside the List/Grid switch, and the tooltip of the column heading while the list is in that order. By size, the smallest files first. Name, Size, Created and Modified are the list's column headings (web.files.column.*), written the same way here. Folders always stay above the files, whatever the order.

web.files.sort.size_desc.note: Files: an order in the Sort by list beside the List/Grid switch, and the tooltip of the column heading while the list is in that order. By size, the largest files first. Name, Size, Created and Modified are the list's column headings (web.files.column.*), written the same way here. Folders always stay above the files, whatever the order.

web.files.sort.sorted.note: Files: read out by screen readers after the order of the list changes; never shown. {order} is the order picked, as the Sort by list writes it (web.files.sort.size_desc: 'Size, largest first'). If 'Sorted by' doesn't read well before it in your language, use a colon instead ('Sorted: Size, largest first').

web.files.toolbar.grid.note: Files: tooltip of the button that shows the folder as a grid of thumbnails.

web.files.toolbar.list.note: Files: tooltip of the button that shows the folder as a list (name, size, dates).

web.files.toolbar.path.note: Files: label before the field holding the folder shown (/Photos/2024/). Keep the colon if your language uses one there.

web.files.toolbar.storage.note: Tooltip and screen-reader name of the third view button in Files' toolbar, next to List (web.files.toolbar.list) and Grid (web.files.toolbar.grid): shows the Storage view, what takes space in the open folder. Use your language's word for storage space; a short word.

web.files.toolbar.view.note: Files: accessibility name of the pair of buttons that switch between the list and the grid of thumbnails.

web.files.upload.done.note: Files: status of a dropped file that was uploaded, in the upload panel. Keep the check mark.

web.files.upload.failed.note: Files: status of a dropped file that couldn't be uploaded, in the upload panel. Keep the cross.

web.files.upload.finished_failed.note: Files: title of the upload panel once every dropped file was tried and some failed. {done} uploaded, {failed} failed.

web.files.upload.progress.note: Files: title of the upload panel while dropped files are sent. {done} is how many are done, {total} how many were dropped.

web.files.upload.reading.note: Files: status of a dropped file waiting to be read and sent, in the upload panel.

web.files.upload.uploaded.note: Files: title of the upload panel once every dropped file was uploaded.

web.files.upload.uploading.note: Files: status shown on each row of the upload panel.

web.files.usage.empty.text: Nothing in this folder takes up space.
web.files.usage.empty.note: Shown in Files' Storage view (the third view, next to List and Grid), which shows what takes space in the open folder: each file and folder in it with a bar, its share of the folder and its size, largest first. in place of the rows when nothing in the folder takes space: it is empty, or holds only empty folders.

web.files.usage.failed.text: Couldn't find out how much space this folder takes.
web.files.usage.failed.note: Shown in Files' Storage view (the third view, next to List and Grid), which shows what takes space in the open folder: each file and folder in it with a bar, its share of the folder and its size, largest first. in place of the rows when the device didn't answer (no connection, no reply) and gave no reason of its own; a Try again button (common.try_again) follows.

web.files.usage.needs_update.text: Your device needs an update to show how much space folders take.
web.files.usage.needs_update.note: Shown in Files' Storage view (the third view, next to List and Grid), which shows what takes space in the open folder: each file and folder in it with a bar, its share of the folder and its size, largest first. in place of the rows when the device's software is too old to say how much space folders take.

web.files.usage.note.text: Sizes are counted file by file: a file kept in two places counts twice, though the device stores it once. Thumbnails and encryption aren't counted, so the totals won't match the storage bar.
web.files.usage.note.note: Footnote under the rows of Files' Storage view (the third view, next to List and Grid), which shows what takes space in the open folder: each file and folder in it with a bar, its share of the folder and its size, largest first.: the sizes are each file's own size. Content stored at two paths is kept once on the device but counted at both; thumbnails (the small previews) and the space encryption adds aren't counted. So the totals differ from the bar that shows how full the device's storage is (in the menu and Settings).

web.files.usage.row_label.note: Screen-reader name of a row in Files' Storage view (the third view, next to List and Grid), which shows what takes space in the open folder: each file and folder in it with a bar, its share of the folder and its size, largest first.. {name} is the file's or folder's name; {size} its size, already formatted with its unit (1.2 GB); {share} is the row's share of the folder, already formatted as a percentage (45%), or web.files.usage.share_small when it is under one per cent. When the folder takes no space at all, {share} is 0%.

web.files.usage.share_small.note: In Files' Storage view (the third view, next to List and Grid), which shows what takes space in the open folder: each file and folder in it with a bar, its share of the folder and its size, largest first.: the share of a file or folder that takes some space but less than one per cent of the folder, in place of a percentage like 45%. Write the per cent sign as your language does. Starts in lowercase in English: it is a value, and it is also put inside web.files.usage.row_label.

web.files.usage.total.note: First line above the rows of Files' Storage view (the third view, next to List and Grid), which shows what takes space in the open folder: each file and folder in it with a bar, its share of the folder and its size, largest first. {size} is the folder's whole size, older versions included (the base of the rows' percentages), already formatted with its unit (1.2 TB); {count} is how many files are under it, at any depth.

web.files.usage.versions.note: Second line above the rows of Files' Storage view (the third view, next to List and Grid), which shows what takes space in the open folder: each file and folder in it with a bar, its share of the folder and its size, largest first., under web.files.usage.total, shown only when the folder keeps older versions of files (in upload-only folders). {size} is how much of the folder's size they take, already formatted with its unit (3.4 GB).

web.files.versions.count.note: Files list: button beside a file with older versions. {count} is how many older versions there are.

web.files.versions.current.note: Files: the first row of a file's versions pop-up, the version in use now.

web.files.versions.hint.text: The file is in an upload-only folder, so each upload to this path kept the one before it.
web.files.versions.hint.note: Files: explanation at the top of a file's versions pop-up.

web.files.versions.replaced.note: Files: a row of a file's versions pop-up. {date} is when that version was replaced by a newer upload, already formatted (9/1/2026, 10:42:07 AM), or a dash when unknown.

web.files.versions.tip.note: Files: tooltip of the button beside a file that opens the list of its older versions (kept because the file is in an upload-only folder).

web.files.versions.title.note: Files: title of the pop-up listing a file's older versions. {name} is the file's name.
